source.title: MiniOneRec: An Open-Source Framework for Scaling Generative Recommendation
source.authors: Xiaoyu Kong; Leheng Sheng; Junfei Tan; Yuxin Chen; Jiancan Wu; An Zhang; Xiang Wang; Xiangnan He

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure graphics are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether loss changes with model size in generative recommendation, a recommendation training regime rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports only a downward trend in loss with size, not fitted exponents or a test of predictions from smaller runs. It does not test compute-optimal allocation, architecture-shape effects, or downstream predictability across model sizes. Other recommender comparisons and ablations do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study varies model size (four Qwen2.5 backbones, 0.5B to 7B) in a generative-recommendation fine-tuning regime and reports how loss changes with size. This bears on V5, the claim that scaling holds in other training regimes such as fine-tuning. The evidence is qualitative only: loss falls monotonically with size. There is no power-law fit, no exponent, and no loss values in the text, and the size range spans only about one order of magnitude.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say they 'systematically validate scaling laws' because larger generative recommenders reach lower training and evaluation losses. They also claim this confirms a parameter-efficiency advantage over embedding-centric recommenders, but they never scale those baselines, so that comparison is asserted, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: A model-size sweep for generative recommendation training losses, rather than language-model pretraining loss scaling; no power-law fitting, small-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.problems: The scaling results are described qualitatively in the supplied text without numerical loss values or fitted power-law parameters. The reported scaling sweep covers four model variants but does not provide their individual sizes in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported for extraction. The paper's recommendation accuracy baselines, transfer experiment, and post-training ablations do not measure the scaling-law versions beyond the loss trends recorded here.

untested.parts: The power-law functional form; any fitted exponent; scaling over several orders of magnitude; data or compute scaling; other modalities, repeated data, and transfer regimes.
Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small runs.
Not tested: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: recommendation accuracy (HR/NDCG) is not reported as a function of model size.
Not tested: no comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: Per-model sizes and loss values behind the scaling curves; these exist only in figure graphics not present in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label was replaced. The lack of a power-law fit is an untested part of V5, not evidence of a qualified effect, so it goes under untested. The supports verdict is weak: four points, a narrow size range, and a confound between parameter count and the pretraining of the Qwen checkpoints.

versions.untested_parts: The reported losses are for generative recommendation training, not held-out language-model pretraining loss.
No smaller-run fit is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is reported.
The study does not vary depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Tests scaling in a generative recommendation training regime only; does not test other modalities, repeated data, or transfer/fine-tuning regimes beyond its recommendation setup, and does not establish a fitted power-law form.
Reports recommendation accuracy comparisons but does not measure downstream-task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or report setup-dependent exponents, disagreement between published laws, or curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: MiniOneRec variants (four variants; individual model names not stated)
rows.size_stated: 0.5B to 7B parameters; individual sizes not stated
rows.stage_stated: SFT; scaling models trained with identical data splits and hyperparameter settings
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss across four model sizes.

conditions.value: Amazon Review; Industrial and Office benchmarks

rows.value: The paper states that final training loss consistently decreases as model size grows; numerical values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.note: The reported direction is consistent with lower loss at larger scale, but no fitted power law or exponent is reported. Individual model sizes and loss values are not stated.
rows.check: The direction of the effect (lower final loss at larger size) is stated without qualification, so for the part of V5 this study can test it is observed, not partial. The missing power-law fit is a gap in the test, not a weaker result; it belongs under untested. Caveats: the measure is fine-tuning training loss, not held-out loss; sizes span 0.5B-7B, about 1.1 orders of magnitude; and the backbones are pretrained Qwen models, so pretraining scale is confounded with parameter count. Individual sizes and loss values are not given in the text.

rows.subject: MiniOneRec variants (four variants; individual model names not stated)
rows.size_stated: 0.5B to 7B parameters; individual sizes not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared evaluation loss during SFT across four model sizes.

conditions.value: Amazon Review; Industrial and Office benchmarks

rows.measure: Evaluation loss; the text describes it as tracked on the SFT training set
rows.value: The paper states that larger models maintain lower evaluation losses through nearly the entire training process and converge more rapidly; numerical values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.note: The trend is explicitly described, but the supplied text gives no numerical curve values or power-law fit. The paper calls this evaluation loss while stating it is recorded on the SFT training set.
rows.check: Larger models are described as having lower loss through nearly all of training, which is the direction V5 expects. The measure is ambiguous: Section 5.2 says the 'evaluation loss' is tracked on the SFT training set, while the introduction calls it held-out evaluation loss. The row should note this contradiction. No values or fit are reported.

relationships.condition: SFT of pretrained Qwen2.5 backbones (0.5B-7B) for SID-based generative recommendation on Amazon Industrial/Office
relationships.reason: Final loss and per-epoch loss fall consistently with size (R1, R2). Only the direction is shown: no power-law fit, about one order of magnitude, values only in figures.
relationships.display_finding: Final and per-epoch losses decreased consistently with backbone size over about one order of magnitude, without a fitted power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
